News.title: Iran leave handwritten note about dead schoolgirls after tense stay in LA
News.content:
Belgium will be looking to step a big step towards qualification for the knockout stages as they take on Iran in Los Angeles. Today’s game on the west coast of the United States is the first-ever meeting between the two nations.

Belgium were involved in an engaging opener in their first game in Group G, drawing 1-1 against Egypt in Seattle as they came from behind to earn a point. A victory today would take them to four points, which would almost guarantee a last-32 spot with a game to go.

“We have analyzed Iran less thoroughly than usual because they are a team that is hard to track in friendly matches,” Belgium boss Rudi Garcia said ahead of the game. “However, we have seen that they had a strong qualifying campaign for the World Cup. We obviously watched them in their first match against New Zealand. They have players we know well and others we are less familiar with since we do not follow Asian teams very closely. But everyone obviously knows [Medhi] Taremi. I am French, so I am also familiar with [Saman] Ghoddos, who played for Amiens.

“They are a team that runs a lot, defends well and is strong on set pieces. So, I would say, regardless of who starts for them or who starts for us, whether they have played together before or not, one thing is certain: we have to be at 100 per cent of our ability tomorrow [today] to beat this Iranian team. So, we are focusing much more on ourselves than on the opponent.”

Belgium will be without Manchester City winger Jeremy Doku, who is out due to illness. Doku has said that he could return home for the birth of his first child should his wife give birth during the tournament.

Iran’s build-up to the tournament was dominated by the conflict between the country and co-hosts the United States linked to the war in the Middle East. They are allowed to fly into the US a day before they have a game but have to leave on the same day as a match under the conditions of their visas. Iran are lodging an official complaint to Fifa about these travel restrictions. Iran were involved in a thriller in their first game of Group G, drawing 2-2 against New Zealand in this stadium. Following that game, their head coach Amir Ghalenoei said that they are the “most oppressed” team at the tournament.

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Freedom day: British passengers on ‘rat-virus’ cruise ship leave lockdown
News.content:
None developed Hantavirus, which has an incubation period of up to six weeks, and they will now all be able to return to their daily lives as normal.

The group were regularly tested by teams from the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) and the NHS throughout the isolation period, The Telegraph understands.

They were also required to take part in daily check-ins with UKHSA behavioural support teams, who monitored their wellbeing.

The agency arranged for groceries to be safely delivered and ensured passengers were able to exercise outdoors during their isolation.

The isolation period was “voluntary” rather than mandated by law, although all passengers are understood to have complied with the measures.

It is also “freedom day” for 125 other passengers repatriated to their home countries, including the US, France, and Australia, and marks the end of an 80-day outbreak that began in early April when a Dutch couple boarded the MV Hondius after travelling in South America.

The pair are thought to have contracted the rare Andes strain of Hantavirus – which can spread to humans through contact with infected rodent droppings – during a birdwatching trip, before boarding the ship in Argentina.

Both later died, along with a German tourist. Three other passengers from the cruise, including a British doctor, were treated in intensive care.

The Andes strain of the virus can spread through close contact, including respiratory droplets produced when an infected person coughs or sneezes.

Cruise ships are often described as “floating Petri dishes” because their enclosed environments and close living quarters provide ideal conditions for infectious diseases to spread.

News.title: Lamine Yamal transforms Spain in demolition of Saudi Arabia
News.content:
Yamal, having missed the final weeks of Barcelona’s title romp in La Liga with injury, was only given 45 minutes as he worked himself back to fitness, but in that half he showed why every left-back in the tournament will be praying they don’t have to come up against him.

By contrast, we will be watching and hoping the fun he brings does not stop. When you tune into a World Cup, you do so hoping the global talents become peacock-proud and put on a show to remind everyone why there is such chatter. How this boy, who is only just a man, obliged.

“I’ve always dreamt of being at a World Cup, and being able to score in my first match as a starter is a dream,” he gasped. “I watched the last World Cup from a classroom so being able to score here with my mum and my family in the stands is a dream come true.”

Many his age are still in classrooms, finishing their final exams before heading to university. Yamal, by contrast, is destined for the stratosphere occupied by the greats. Don’t get sucked into comparisons with those who have gone before, simply enjoy watching how his journey unfolds.

Remarkably, Yamal – who became the eighth youngest scorer in World Cup history at 18 years and 343 days – was not the youngest player to score at this tournament, that particular footnote falling to Ibrahim Mbaye, the Senegal forward from Paris St-Germain, who is 200 days his junior.

News.title: Crisis-hit England blown away inside 48 minutes ahead of Stokes return
News.content:
The Lord’s win should have changed the mood around England but now we are back in Sydney, their reputation a shambles. Rob Key, the director of cricket, faces awkward questions over the way he communicated the curfew. The Ashes was a failure of planning and professionalism and this is another example of the regime’s looseness. It is just not a professional, high-performance environment. It cannot go on if they are to be serious candidates to win back the Ashes next summer. On Key’s watch, discipline has fallen apart, the team’s public image is lower than ever and wins have dried up. This was England’s sixth loss in eight Tests and when they play a decent side such as New Zealand, they do not have the game to win consistently. Key needs a series win, badly.

Key and McCullum are two men trying to be something they are not. They do not like meetings, rules and regulations and process, but because of the Ashes hammering they were forced to take on a more serious approach. If Richard Gould and Richard Thompson, the chief executive and chair, wanted the whip to be cracked they needed to bring in new management but they blinked. Key retains their support and insiders at the England and Wales Cricket Board blame Stokes and Atkinson, but what does it say about the captain’s respect for the director of cricket and coach that he was so willing to throw the new rules in the bin? It is a sign that the Ashes scars will never heal.

Bazball stirred the nation at Trent Bridge in 2022 and one of the men who felt the full force of it was Matt Henry as Jonny Bairstow smacked him into the River Trent. Now Henry could bring it all crashing down on a pitch in Nottingham that will dry after the heatwave and probably nip like the one at the Oval.

Sports.title: Porn star wears eye-popping outfit at World Cup clash as fans say ‘no way she was allowed to wear that in public’
Sports.content:
WORLD CUP fans were left stunned when a porn star was spotted posing outside a stadium with just a scarf covering her breasts.

Raissa Bellini jetted into Miami for Uruguay’s 2-2 draw with tournament debutants Cape Verde.





And the Italian, 37, left little to the imagination when she arrived for the Group H showdown in the Florida sunshine.

Raissa posed for photos with fans while only wearing figure-hugging jean shorts and a World Cup scarf.

She was then seen inside the stadium, which is the home of NFL giants Miami Dolphins, sporting a low-cut tank top.

And Raissa came under fire from World Cup fans when snaps and footage emerged on social media.



One said: “No way she was allowed to wear that in public. What’s going on in the world these days?”

Another added: “Parents take their children to see these matches. They need to ban any and every form of nudity within and outside the stadiums.”

A third chimed in: “How do these people even get entry to the stadium?”

A fourth noted: “I feel like if I did this in the UK I would get arrested.”



Raissa spent five years working as a stewardess on luxury yachts, where she mingled with billionaires, big-name celebrities and high-powered businessmen.

But, since moving into the porn industry, she has seen her number of social media followers skyrocket.

She saw Cape Verde edge towards booking their place in the knockout stages of the World Cup.

The minnows bagged a point against Uruguay after pulling off an almighty shock by holding Spain to a goalless draw last week.



Cape Verde will go head-to-head with Saudi Arabia in their final Group H showdown later this week.

Spain and Uruguay, who are currently first and second respectively, are set to meet at the same time in Guadalajara.

Sports.title: Scotland fans sing along as ROBOT dances in kilt with traffic cone on its head ahead of World Cup clash vs Brazil
Sports.content:
SCOTLAND fans have been loving life at the World Cup, and have even recruited a robotic supporter.

The Tartan Army are gearing up for their crunch do-or-die World Cup Group C finale against Brazil, knowing a loss could send them home.





Scots who made the journey over to watch Steve Clarke‘s side saw them win 1-0 against Haiti before they suffered a 1-0 loss to Morocco.

And ahead of the Brazil game in Miami, Scots were seen partying alongside a dancing ROBOT wearing a kilt and a traffic cone on its head.

The cone prank, a tradition dating back to the 1980s, became a common sight in Boston, where Scotland played it’s first two World Cup games.

The atmosphere they have generated has earned them many fans, so much so that amazingly the antics were celebrated by Boston officials.



And so fond are the feelings they generated that the Boston Globe, one of the biggest and oldest newspapers in the United States, dedicated an emotional goodbye to them as they head for Miami.

They said: “Dear Tartan Army.

“You came for the World Cup, but gave us something more.

“For a week, you turned train stations into singalongs, Fenway into a football ground, and an ordinary June into something we’ll be talking about for years.

“Boston has hosted championships, parades, and celebrations of every kind.

“But we’ve never hosted guests quite like you all.

“Thank you for the laughter, the bagpipes, and the memories.

“So will the songs, but we’ll never forget the joy you brought to our city.



“The Boston Globe.”

Sports.title: Taco-eating World Cup duck Merlin ATTACKS Mexican president after becoming viral sensation at tournament
Sports.content:
VIRAL World Cup sensation Merlin the Duck took a peck at Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum after being introduced.

Merlin has shot to fame since beating spotted wearing a Mexico shirt during street celebrations of the co-hosts’ 2-0 win over South Africa.





Fans immediately took to Merlin, with the patriotic duck having become the World Cup’s unofficial mascot.

Such is Merlin’s newfound fame, that he was invited to meet President Sheinbaum.

And he quickly stole the show at the 63-year-old’s morning press conference in Mexico City.

Merlin waddled over to Sheinbaum, to the delight of onlookers.

As she attempted to pet him, however, he attempted to take a peck at her.

Luckily Sheinbaum quickly drew her hand away and was not injured in the incident.



Merlin’s owner Carla Gomez subsequently spoke of her pride at being invited to meet her country’s president.

Gomez said: “We feel very honoured to be here with the president, it is an honour for ⁠us to stand before you and for the whole world to see the ​beautiful side of Mexico.”

WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

Sheinbaum also gushed over new national hero Merlin.

She said: “Today we brought the ​family that has Merlin the duck as their pet, because he has been a symbol of the World Cup, a symbol of what Mexican families stand for, of who we are as Mexican families, and that is above all else, it is ⁠what the world is seeing from Mexico today.”



Two-year-old Merlin loves being treated to a taco on Sundays.

Gomez, meanwhile is a street vendor and is proud to be a working class Mexican.

Merlin was gifted to her by a customer and loves to help out.

Gomez added of Merlin’s newfound fame: “It has been the best thing that has happened to us in this life”.

Sports.title: England and Scotland fans party side-by-side in Boston as Three Lions fans find bars drunk dry ahead of clash with Ghana
Sports.content:
ENGLAND and Scotland fans partied side-by-side in Boston yesterday as Three Lions fans arrived to find bars drunk dry.

More than 30,000 Scots flooded in and drained pubs during a non-stop eight-day party while watching their two games in the US East Coast city.





England fans faced a struggle to find bars still serving yesterday as thousands began flooding in yesterday ahead of today’s crucial second Group L clash with Ghana.

But fans from the two Auld Enemy nations enjoyed an unexpected truce as England fans prepared to whoop it up together at wild World Cup watering holes.

Scots – gutted after losing 1-0 to Morocco on Friday and needing a point to stay in the tournament against Brazil – grudgingly wished their old foes well yesterday.

England fans sporting Three Lions shirts and kilted Scots happily partied together in Hennessy’s Bar in the bustling centre of Boston yesterday.

North London banker Nick Soutar, 29, said: “We have a reputation for being old enemies but we’ve been anything but since I arrived – the Scots are great fun.

“I’ve seen no trouble whatsoever and the rivalry is very friendly.

“The beer may be running out but there’s no shortage of party action. It’s been brilliant.”

““We were playing keepy uppy in the street with the Scotland fans and the locals. It was a cracking atmosphere.”



Asked whether he would wish England well should Scotland fail to qualify for the knockout rounds yet again, Gordon Forsyth, 67, from Inverness laughed: “You’ll have to speak to my lawyer before I answer that!”

Gordon – a Scottish Water tanker driver – added: “The atmosphere here has been brilliant and we’ve been having beers and laughs with the England fans.

“All the Scots are just happy to be here for the first time in years and hoping to stay for as long as possible.”



England fan Mark Richardson, a 29-year-old insurance underwriter from Enfield, North London laughed: “Lots of beer has run out but the Scots didn’t quite manage to drink it all and there’s still enough for a party.

“We’ve forgiven them for that and are having a ball with them while they’re here – which probably won’t be for much longer.

“But England are going all the way – and our fans are here to stay.”

Sports.title: What happens if France vs Iraq in the World Cup 2026 is postponed?
Sports.content:
FRANCE against Iraq has been suspended due to a severe storm.

Les Bleus were leading 1-0 via a Kylian Mbappe goal when a heavy downpour hit Philadelphia.





Supporters were forced to evacuate the stands and the game has been halted indefinitely.

Fifa might be forced to postpone the match and here are the rules if they do.

What happens if a World Cup 2026 match is postponed?

World Cup regulations state that a game must restart on a future date if it is called off halfway through.

The match would begin again from the same time it stopped rather than be re-played from the beginning.

Therefore, if a game is postponed in the 78th minute, players will return another day to play the remaining 12 minutes and stoppage time.

The same players must restart the game and no bonus subs or changes are permitted.

The date, time and location of the resumption will be decided by World Cup chiefs.

Fifa rules state:



a) The match shall recommence at the minute at which play was interrupted rather than being replayed in full, and with the same scoreline

The match shall recommence where play was stopped when the match was interrupted (e.g. with a free kick, throw‑in, goal kick, corner kick, penalty kick, etc.). If the match was abandoned while the ball was still in play, it shall restart with a dropped ball from the position of the ball when play was stopped.

b) The match shall recommence with the same players on the pitch and substitutes available as when the match was abandoned.

c) No additional substitutes may be added to the list of players on the start list.

d) The teams can make only the number of substitutions to which they were still entitled when the match was abandoned.

e) Players sent off during the abandoned match cannot be replaced.

f) Any disciplinary measures imposed before the match was abandoned will be dealt with in accordance with the FIFA Disciplinary Code.

g) The kick‑off time, date, location and any other matter shall be decided by FIFA.

What if a World Cup 2026 match is delayed?

Fifa must follow rules set by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

If lightning is detected within eight miles of a stadium, the game will be halted with players leaving the field and fans told to shelter out of their seats.

After a bolt of lightning strikes, a 30-minute countdown begins that resets every time another happens.

We must go half an hour without lightning for the match to resume.

There is no maximum time for a delay.



Fifa state they will judge each weather suspension on a case by case basis.

During the Club World Cup held in the US last year, Chelsea vs Benfica was halted for two hours due to a storm.

Sports.title: What time will France vs Iraq restart at World Cup?
Sports.content:
THE World Cup clash between France and Iraq has been DELAYED.

Severe storms down at the Philadelphia Stadium saw the field drenched.





Players and fans were left soaked as the wild weather battered the City of Brotherly Love.

During halftime of the clash, supporters were warned to go inside due to thunderstorms in the area.

The wind is understood to a major issue in the stadium.

That came at the start of the break, meaning there was a 15 minute interval.



Due to Fifa’s World Cup rules, a delay of 30 minutes must be observed when lightning is in the area.

However, it was believed the players will start warming up again at 6.40pm ET (11.40pm UK).

That did NOT happen, but by 7.32pm ET (12.32am UK), the players were back out warming up.

That means the France against Iraq showdown will now restart at 7.50pm ET (12.50am UK time).



That could be extended if there is even more lightning or bad weather in the area.

Our live blog will have ALL the updates HERE.

Sports.title: Germany star, 18, gets over World Cup heartbreak with model girlfriend, 22, as he shares busty pic of her eating pasta
Sports.content:
LENNART KARL has shared a stunning snap of girlfriend Zoe Kappele as he desperately attempts to get over his World Cup heartbreak.

The Bayern Munich sensation, 18, was included in Germany’s 26-man squad after a breakthrough season in the Bundesliga.





But Karl’s World Cup dreams were left in tatters when he suffered a thigh injury days before the tournament got underway.

And the teenage talent shared a daring snap of his model girlfriend on social media after trying to take the summer extravaganza off his mind.

The photo, which was uploaded onto Instagram Stories, shows 22-year-old Zoe wearing a low-cut red dress.

And the blonde beauty puckered up while tucking into some spaghetti at a fancy restaurant.

Bild report the moment was captured at Sorriso, an Italian restaurant at the five-star Lujo hotel in Turkey.

Karl and his loved-up partner jetted out to Bodrum, Turkey, for a dream holiday after it became clear he could not feature at the World Cup.



Zoe has a huge social following where she shares travel content and shows off her dance moves.

The model also launched a clothing brand called Camogliii in 2024, allowing her to rake in cash.



Germany have already booked their place in the knockout stages of the World Cup despite being rocked by Karl’s injury at the eleventh hour.

They came from behind to notch a last-gasp 2-1 win over Ivory Coast on Saturday.

Former Brighton striker Deniz Undav came off the bench to bag a brace after Franck Kessie’s opener.

But the win came at a cost because Nico Schlotterbeck was ruled out for the rest of the tournament.



Former Chelsea defender Antonio Rudiger is expected to profit from the Borussia Dortmund man’s absence.

Germany got their pursuit of World Cup glory underway with a 7-1 thumping of minnows Curacao last week.

Sports.title: World Cup star Micky van de Ven’s stunning English model girlfriend puts on busty display in low-cut top
Sports.content:
MICKY VAN DE VEN’S stunning girlfriend left fans jaw-dropped as she wore a low-cut top.

English model Ella Buffin has been cheering on her hunky fella as he stars for the Netherlands in North America.





Tottenham captain Van de Ven, 25, starred in both of their World Cup Group F games – a 2-2 draw with Japan and 5-1 win over Sweden.

But in between games Ella, 24, has been tending to her legion of Instagram followers.

She has 137,000 on Instagram, while she has a further 710,000 on TikTok.

The influencer made her romance with 6ft 4in defender official recently, and the pair follow each other on Instagram.

In exclusive pictures shared by The Sun, Ella and Van de Ven were seen enjoying a romantic holiday together in Marbella, Spain, before he joined his team-mates in camp for the World Cup.

The couple enjoyed a three-hour meal together at The Grill.



An onlooker said: “They looked absolutely smitten.

“Micky was doe-eyed all night.

“It was such a beautiful setting and they looked so happy.”

The source added: “They talked and laughed all night before heading back to their room shortly before midnight.”

The couple earlier spent the day lounging around the luxury pool before a long lunch at trendy Nobu, a few minutes walk away on the beach.



Sporty Ella, a netball and athletics nut, also donned a white number during their getaway as the new couple played a round of golf.

Recent trips abroad include Santorini, Dubai, Mykonos, Ibiza, Bali and Rhodes.

It is a far cry from her days as a pupil at £45,000-a-year Repton School in Derbyshire whose alumni includes Sun columnist Jeremy Clarkson and Charlie and the Chocolate Factory author Roald Dahl.



She went on to study fashion at Manchester Metropolitan University and has since posed for brands including Asos, Adidas, Goose and Gander, Cernucci and Outcast Clothing.

The well-spoken Derby County supporter is also a huge tennis fan and a regular at Wimbledon and the Australian Open.

Sports.title: World Cup LIVE: FIFA cancel hydration break after France weather chaos
Sports.content:
France's match against Iraq in Philadelphia this evening could face delays as a weather warning has been issued for lightning and isolated tornadoes

The clash between France and Iraq at Philadelphia's Lincoln Financial Field was delayed by two hours due to extreme weather in the United States.

A NEXT weather alert was issued for Monday in the Philadelphia area due to thunderstorms and heavy rain forecast for the afternoon and night. "Several thunderstorms are expected to become severe, with damaging winds, intense lightning, and a risk of isolated tornadoes," CBS News reports.

Lightning was present as the half-time whistle blew, with players forced to wait until at least 15 minutes after the last flash to return to the pitch. Play did eventually resume with the second half water break cancelled due to the delay.

It comes as Argentina put Austria to the sword 2-0 in Monday's opening evening game at the 2026 World Cup. Lionel Messi missed a spot kick early into the encounter, but atoned just before half-time with a rocketed strike into the far corner of Alexander Schlager's goal.

The seasoned Inter Miami sensation struck once more at the game's death to secure his nation's fate in the knockout stages of the competition, setting a new record for overall goals scored at the World Cup (17).

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel provides Bukayo Saka injury update as England boss given selection headache
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel provides Bukayo Saka injury update as England boss given selection headache

Bukayo Saka was only fit to feature as a substitute against Croatia but could get the nod from the start when England face Ghana on Tuesday

View 2 Images Saka is in contention to start against Ghana (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Thomas Tuchel says Declan Rice is now one of the best midfielders in the world. Rice is set to win his 75th cap against Ghana on Tuesday night in Boston and has been given a glowing tribute by his international boss.

‌



England boss Tuchel said: “The point where he is now is one of the very best midfielders in the world. You see a humble, humble footballer, humble, ready to be a team player, ready every day to give energy into the good quality into the group and just ready to learn and learn every day.

‌



“So his career makes him one of the very best at the moment. So proud peace coach.”

‌



Tuchel says Bukayo Saka is fit to start against Ghana but may not actually get the green light because there is such competition for places.

Declan Rice pays Harry Kane the ultimate compliment after blistering start to World Cup READ MORE :

Thomas Tuchel sends brutal warning to England stars as FIFA rule change takes effect READ MORE :

But Saka’s return to full fitness after an Achilles injury is a major boost for England ahead of the the rest of the tournament.

Tuchel added: "It's another big thing on the right wing between Noni Madueke and Bukayo Saka and the beautiful thing is they do it for Arsenal as well. Bukayo is getting better and better, feels no more pain and he is ready to go - without telling you if he starts or comes from the bench.

‌



"Everyone has trained, everyone is available. No matter whether it's Marc (Guehi) in defence or Marcus (Rashford) and Bukayo (Saka), they all bought into it, the team as starters or coming on from the bench.”

Tuchel did a U-turn by saying he does not like hydration breaks - even though originally he said they were necessary because of the climate.

But England did lose momentum against Croatia last week and Tuchel said that is a problem in this tournament. Tuchel added: “I think it interrupts and changes the identity of the football match much more than I thought.

‌



View 2 Images Tuchel has a selection headache for the Ghana clash (Image: Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

“I had, of course, hydration breaks before. They were needed, but they were shorter. They were shorter and they were just in a few matches.

“Now it is a point of fairness to every team. Now it breaks the match almost in four quarters. I think it changes the characteristics of the match more than I thought. I like it as a coach, of course, to have influence and have my team together.

‌



“But overall I think I like football more when it's played in one go. It builds momentum, it's part of the game. It's hard to build momentum and it's hard to keep the momentum. It's just like the battle on the field between the players and the teams.

“It plays out over a longer period of time. It just adds to the characteristic of a beautiful game. This takes away from it. But in terms of fairness, of course it makes sense that everyone gets it.”

Sports.title: Declan Rice pays Harry Kane the ultimate compliment after blistering start to World Cup
Sports.content:
Declan Rice pays Harry Kane the ultimate compliment after blistering start to World Cup

Harry Kane stacks up against any other striker in the World Cup according to Declan Rice after the England skipper scored twice in their opener against Croatia

View 2 Images Rice insists Kane is right up there with the best in the world (Image: Getty Images)

Declan Rice says Harry Kane is such a legendary figure in English football that he will tell his kids he played with him. England midfielder Rice clearly believes the Bayern Munich superstar stands up against any of the strikers at the World Cup.

‌



And Rice admits that even he gets star struck at times by just how good Kane is while he also insisted England can go all the way this summer.

‌



Rice said: “He's one of those players that can tell the kids when they're older that they got to play with Harry Kane. For me, that's unbelievable.

‌



“He's one of them players that I'm very fortunate to have. One, he's our captain. But two, how he leads by example every day and how he pushes in training.

“It's not a surprise to me how good he is just because of the goals he scores in training and what he's been doing at Bayern Munich and what he's been doing in an England shirt. It's been an honour to play with him.”

Lionel Messi becomes World Cup record scorer as Argentina icon breaks Miroslav Klose record READ MORE :

Predicted England XI vs Ghana: Thomas Tuchel has made up his mind on three big calls READ MORE :

England made a winning start to their Group but Rice says they will face a tough test against Ghana - but will be determined to win and says they believe they can beat anyone.

‌



Rice said: “We are just as motivated if not more motivated to win. Harry spoke about it earlier that we haven’t always had a great result in the second game so we have to get that right.

“If you look back on the second half, it was probably the best half of football we’ve played under Thomas.

“That performance was the benchmark now and if we keep playing like that then we will be a match for anyone and we should have confidence in our ability and believe we can beat anyone in this tournament.”

‌



View 2 Images Declan Rice and Harry Kane during the clash against Croatia (Image: Getty Images)

Rice also says he will face a difficult battle against former Arsenal team mate Thomas Partey who he will be up against in midfield.

Rice added: “I played against Thomas, so I played with Thomas Arsenal. A really good player, but also I've played against a lot of the Ghana team. And like I said from the clips, I know what they're going to bring.

"They're going to bring strength and pace. They want to catch us out on the counter attack. So yeah, we need to be ready for everything. But also, we have played against a lot of them. Players already know what's going to be coming tomorrow.”

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel sends brutal warning to England stars as FIFA rule change takes effect
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel sends brutal warning to England stars as FIFA rule change takes effect

England will face off against Ghana on Tuesday night looking to book their place in the World Cup knockout stages, but Thomas Tuchel wants his players to remain vigilant

View 2 Images England manager Thomas Tuchel during training in Kansas City

Thomas Tuchel has told his players to keep “calm” heads - because their World Cup could be over in an instant.

‌



FIFA have brought in a set of strict new rules for referees in this tournament and Paraguay's Miguel Almirón made history by becoming the first player to be sent off for covering his mouth in a confrontational situation.

‌



England boss Tuchel says his players must stay focused and not get carried away otherwise they could come unstuck by a moment of bad discipline.

‌



Tuchel said: “It always can change in an instant. You're always just one red card away from a completely new situation, this can always happen.

“The best thing is to be calm and focused and in good spirits within the group to be ready to face adversity. The first test game in the goals we conceded against Croatia and some other stuff will come, we just don't know what.

World Cup weather rules: What happens if storms interrupt play with France vs Iraq at risk READ MORE :

FIFA issue statement after France and Brazil stars complain about World Cup final venue READ MORE :

“I don't want to talk about it too much and prepare for something but something else is round the corner. Maybe nothing is around the corner so why even put it out there? Maybe nothing is round the corner and we do it and we will be in control. Let's see.

‌



“The most important is to be aware that things can get sticky, things can get tough, things can get difficult and have the right mindset and also be relaxed and trustful enough within the group to have an answer for it when it comes.”

Things had threatened to get sticky during the opener vs Croatia in Dallas, after surrendering two leads in the first half.

That led to some home truths both in the dressing room and to to the watching nation. And Tuchel says he “loved” Anthony Barry’s half-time TV rant.

‌



View 2 Images Anthony Barry slammed England for their first-half performance vs Croatia (Image: Getty Images)

Barry let rip into England’s first half performance against Croatia live on TV calling it “complicated and confusing” with some “fearful patterns.”

It raised eyebrows because it was so brutally honest but England assistant coach Barry will carry on doing the half time TV interviews through the tournament.

‌



And Tuchel gave him his blessing and stamp of approval even though he admitted he has not watched his back but trusts Barry implicitly.

Tuchel said: “Everyone is speaking about this! Yes, it was great. We loved it. I’m so happy if he does that at half-time — and then I don’t have to do it!

‌



“But why would you say ‘will I allow it to happen?’ Do you think I need to do that?! I’m so happy if he speaks. And you see the quality.

“The guy is a top coach. And he is an inspiration, and he pushes me, and helps me and supports me. It’s just top level.

“I haven’t heard it. But I hear a lot of people speaking, so he gets a lot of banter for it. I can imagine it makes sense what he said, and he spoke hopefully from his heart and from his knowledge because he’s just a top coach.”

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham's status in England team clear as Thomas Tuchel explains 'tricky' Ghana plan
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham is now showing his “full potential” as he reaches a landmark for England.

That is the view of Thomas Tuchel who says the connection between Bellingham and Harry Kane could be England’s path to World Cup glory.

Bellingham is set to win his 50th cap against Ghana, which is a staggering achievement bearing in mind he only turns 23 on June 29.

Real Madrid star Bellingham was sensational against Croatia and his link-up with Kane was highlighted by FIFA’s technical study group because of their understanding. Bellingham was singled out by FIFA analyst Paolo Wanchope for being “very intelligent” and Kane’s ability to drop deep was something “not ever seen before” when it came to their movement.

‌



England clearly have two of their best players in the world right now - and Tuchel praised how they have come together and how it has got the best out of Bellingham.

Get the latest World Cup 2026 news in your inbox with our Make Football Great Again newsletter

FIFA issue statement after France and Brazil stars complain about World Cup final venue READ MORE :

World Cup pundit makes disgusting racist comments live on TV towards Belgium star READ MORE :

Tuchel said Declan Rice and Elliot Anderson were also important but, most tellingly, he also praised the way Bellingham bought into the team ethic which may just destroy any notion of any lingering doubts. Three Lions boss Tuchel said: “In general I saw a strong team performance, I saw the full potential of Jude and the full commitment.

“There is no doubt that a game and competition like this brings out the best in him but it needed improvement, the connection between Jude and Harry, the connection between Jude and Declan and Elliot, it needs improvement and needed improvement and it's a big step.

‌



“Jude played fully into our idea and was fully committed to the team idea and team spirit and to play in full cohesion with everyone else. He was very important, super reliable.”

England really came good against Croatia and, in the second half, they produced a performance to match against anything seen so far at this World Cup. But Tuchel admitted the “tricky part” is to make sure they can do that from the start against Ghana, rather than need a gee-up after a sloppy first half as they did against Croatia.

View 3 Images Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane have a good understanding (Image: Photo by Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images))

Tuchel said: “That is a tricky part, to keep the level up but first of all, I am very happy because we found an answer to adversity. We conceded in a very tricky moment, last shot of the first half and then came up with the best 25 minutes, or best 30 minutes as an answer when we were very, very strong. The team knows that and we showed that.

‌



“We have, of course, we saw the physical input, we saw the ball wins, we saw the chances and we still have stuff to improve. I think it is important to learn from all that and the beautiful thing is that the things that were not so good we do not need to amend anything new, we just need to do our stuff better from the first half.

“Now the problem is that we expect a completely different opponent and style of play. I expect more ball possession. I expect Ghana to rely on counter-attacks because they are very physical, very fast and dangerous in counter-attacks.

“There will be different topics to take care about without losing our momentum, without losing our passion. And still have the spirit and that we are courageous enough to go for it.”

View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel wants a more complete performance from England vs Ghana (Image: Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

‌



But Tuchel insisted that there is still major room for improvement, especially defensively. They shipped two goals and looked rusty and nervous against Croatia. That has been the target to iron out since then in training and Tuchel even claimed conceding goals against Croatia may have been a blessing in disguise.

Tuchel added: “We need to do things better. I think defensively we dropped a little too deep from a middle block into a low block and deep block, which is, in itself, not a problem, but we went a bit too early. Maybe it is good that we conceded, because it just tells us ‘let’s not do this again’. It makes no sense, it’s not us, it doesn’t play to our strengths.

“So we need to manage these ball wins better. And in ball possession there is also stuff to improve. When do we accelerate the game, and how do we give the man on the ball more options in the gaps and show a bit more confidence into what makes us strong?

“That’s the beauty of it: we don’t need to invent anything new. Of course, there are things to improve and the team knows it. There will always be things to improve in any match. But I was also very clear to the team: we deserved this win.

‌



“We had a well-deserved win against a top-ten opponent [Croatia were 11th when England played them] of the World Cup. And we have a lot of positives to take away, and I expect a very different team and a very different set-up now. And we need to improve especially our structure with the ball to be ready to defend counter-attacks before they become dangerous.”

Sports.title: Arsenal stance on signing Julian Alvarez after Argentina star drops transfer bombshell
Sports.content:
Arsenal stance on signing Julian Alvarez after Argentina star drops transfer bombshell

Julian Alvarez has made it clear he wants to leave Atletico Madrid following Argentina's 2-0 World Cup win over Austria

View 2 Images Arsenal admire Julian Alvarez but a summer transfer deal remains highly unlikely

Arsenal target Julian Alvarez wants to join Barcelona and only Barcelona after communicating his desire to leave Atletico Madrid.

‌



After weeks of speculation, which included a monstrous £129million rejected transfer bid from Real Madrid, Alvarez has now publicly spelled declared that he is keen to pursue a new challenge.

‌



While he did not mention Barcelona by name, they are his primary destination of choice and he's hopeful the two clubs will be able to reach an agreement over his services.

‌



Barca have already had one proposal, worth £86.4m, rebuffed. That sparked a series of ugly statements from Atleti, who insisted that the player had a long-term contract and that they would not sell to their rivals.

Thomas Partey breaks silence after World Cup visa scandal as Arsenal stars sent message READ MORE :

Arsenal handed huge transfer incentive as true impact of Premier League title laid bare READ MORE :

Ideally, if Atleti were to offload Alvarez, they would favour doing business with a non-Spanish side but Alvarez is not keen on a return to England where he already won two Premier League titles plus numerous other trophies with Manchester City.

PSG would also be ready to make a big financial commitment to sign Alvarez should he signal his willingness to move to France. That is currently viewed as unlikely, also.

‌



Mirror Football understands that Arsenal have already pushed hard to sign Alvarez this summer, per sources with knowledge of the secret talks that took place with Barca chief Deco at the Torre Melina hotel in Catalonia on May 27.

During those conversations, it was mentioned that the Premier League champions were trying to land Alvarez, who was previously signed by Gunners sporting director Andrea Berta at Atletico.

Politely, the Premier League champions were told by the player's camp that he is desperate to join Barca and was not willing to consider rival offers.

‌



After a prolonged period of silence, Alvarez has now made it clear he wants out of Atletico, where he has a contract until 2030.

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez wants to join Barcelona from Atletico Madrid (Image: Getty)

He said at the AT&T Stadium after Lionel Messi's double downed Austria : “This isn’t the time to talk about this, but I can’t hide either; I try to be an honest person. I spoke with the people at Atlético Madrid, and I think the best thing for everyone is a transfer. I want to fulfil my dream.”

‌



Mirror Football also understands Alvarez's long-standing agent Fernando Hidalgo is currently supporting his client in North America.

Arsenal were also previously interested in signing the 26-year-old when he departed Manchester City but he is keen to remain in Spain having failed to win a trophy in either of his first two seasons with Atletico.

His relationship with boss Diego Simeone is said to have deteriorated and equally, he is believed to be frustrated by the way he was treated after putting his body on the line in the Champions League semi-final against the Gunners.

‌



Alvarez rolled his ankle during the first leg and required an injection to play in the return fixture at the Emirates and because of that issue, he was not deemed fit enough to start Argentina's World Cup opener against Algeria in Kansas City.

Arsenal's only chance of landing Alvarez now is if Barcelona cannot agree on a deal and the situation becomes so untenable that Alvarez wants out of Atletico at all costs.

Sports.title: France vs Iraq World Cup match suspended as emergency action taken
Sports.content:
France vs Iraq World Cup match suspended as emergency action taken

The Group I FIFA World Cup clash between France and Iraq has been halted at half-time at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia due to the weather

View 2 Images The big screen shows a weather warning at Philadelphia Stadium (Image: (Dan Mullan/Getty Images))

France’s group stage clash with Iraq was delayed mid-match due to lightning in the area. Although the game started as planned, with Kylian Mbappe giving France the lead after just 14 minutes, the match, being played at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, was halted at half-time.

‌



Shortly before the break heavy rain began to fall, and with lightning activity approaching, supporters were also told to "exit the open seating areas" of the ground during the interval. FIFA initially confirmed the start of the second half would be delayed by at least 15 minutes as player and fan safety was prioritised.

‌



But in the end, it was nearly two hours before the action got back underway. And speaking to French TV during the delay, Les Bleus boss Didier Deschamps said: "I've stopped giving the players any news because it keeps changing every 30 seconds.”

‌



Confirming the delay, FIFA said in a statement: "Due to adverse weather conditions in Philadelphia, including the risk of lightning in the vicinity of the stadium, the Fifa World Cup match between France and Iraq has been suspended.

"A 30-minute break has been announced. However, the situation is still being observed to determine if further delays are anticipated.

Peter Schmeichel claims record-breaking Lionel Messi goal should NOT have stood READ MORE :

Lionel Messi recovers from penalty shocker to write yet more World Cup history READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"Fifa will follow the safety protocols established by the local authorities, and the match will resume as soon as it is safe to do so. The safety and security of all individuals is Fifa's priority. We thank all fans for their understanding and cooperation."

While the BBC’s Kelly Cates said: "There is a delay to the start of the second-half, there's what they call lightning activity in the area around the stadium in Philadelphia. So they're going to wait until that passes.

"Fans are being asked to take shelter outside of the stadium bowl itself. There are really strong safety protocols in place in the United States.

‌



"So they're just going to go get everybody safe, and then the minute there hasn't been any lightning activity for 15 minutes, the players will come out and then they will warm up for 15 minutes, and then the second-half will get underway. Fingers crossed, we're hoping that the storm is going to pass in plenty of time."

View 2 Images Kylian Mbappe opens the scoring against Iraq (Image: Getty Images)

Lauren Lambrugo, chief operating officer of Philadelphia Soccer 2026, revealed ahead of the tournament the protocol in the event of a match being postponed due to inclement weather. "They'll start to evacuate the stadium to the main concourse and seek emergency shelter," he said. "And then it has to wait 30 minutes prior to them bringing everybody back on the field.”

‌



Severe storms took place in Philadelphia ahead of kick-off, with supporters at one point told not to make their way to the stadium due to the conditions. And France boss Deschamps was asked at his pre-match press conference on Sunday if he was worried about the prospect of heavy rain for their second match of the tournament.

He said: “We have played in the heat (at MetLife) so, if there is some rain, good, because the grass will be faster and the quality will be better, much better than the one in New York. The pitch in New York was really tough — it took a lot out of the players’ muscles.”

Sports.title: Carlson helps Glamorgan to long-awaited County Championship win over Surrey
Sports.content:
Glamorgan captain Kiran Carlson steered his side to a long-awaited win over Surrey in the Rothesay County Championship in Cardiff.

Their seven-wicket win was the Welsh side's first red-ball success against their opponents on home soil since 1983 and dealt Surrey their second defeat of the season.

Tom Lawes reached 66 not out as Surrey added a creditable 49 to their overnight total to set Glamorgan 195 to win.

Sports.title: New Rangers boss McInnes faces ban for opening games
Sports.content:
Derek McInnes faces being banned from the touchline in his opening domestic games as Rangers manager after being hit with a disciplinary charge over criticism of match officials.

McInnes has been cited by the Scottish Football Association compliance officer over remarks made in the wake of Motherwell's late defeat by Celtic in the penultimate fixture of last season.

The then Hearts boss had criticised the penalty decision which led to Celtic's match-winner with the last kick of the game. Hearts were in a closely-contested Scottish Premiership title race with Celtic at the time, which they eventually lost on the final day of the season at their title rivals.

If found guilty, McInnes would miss Rangers' Scottish Premiership opener at Dundee United, which is live on Sky Sports on July 31 - and could then miss a further three fixtures.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hearts boss Derek McInnes was left disappointed by the decision to award Celtic a penalty for handball against Motherwell

Motherwell and Fir Park midfielder Elliot Watt have also been issued with the same charge.

Motherwell face a fine of between £1,000 and £100,000 if found guilty while the minimum punishment for individuals is a four-match ban.

They have all been accused of breaching a rule which forbids criticism which indicates "bias or incompetence" on match officials or impinges on their characters.

McInnes described referee John Beaton's decision to award a penalty for handball against Sam Nicholson - on the advice of video assistant Andrew Dallas - as "actually quite disgusting".

He added after his side's 3-0 win over Falkirk: "I shouldn't be commenting on another game, but having seen that, it feels like us against everybody."

Celtic were facing the challenge of beating leaders Hearts 3-0 on the final day before Kelechi Iheanacho converted the penalty and they ultimately won the title in the closing moments of the season by overturning a one-point deficit and coming from behind with a 3-1 win.

Motherwell have been cited as a club in the wake of social media content, which included the phrase "as the world of football mocks our game".

Watt described the penalty award as the "worst VAR decision in history" on his X account.

All three hearings will be heard on July 16 by a judicial panel convened by the SFA.

Sports.title: Messi makes scoring history with double to send Argentina through
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi broke the World Cup scoring record as Argentina beat Austria 2-0 in Dallas to secure their place in the knockout stages.

Messi had missed an early penalty after VAR intervened to award a spot-kick for a foul on Lautaro Martinez but the 38-year-old Argentina captain could not be denied for long, scoring with a trademark finish from Facundo Medina's low cross in the first half.

Messi's first goal brought up 17 in the World Cup - moving him clear of Miroslav Klose as the top scorer in the tournament's history. He added a second in stoppage-time to take his tally to five in just two Group J fixtures after his hat-trick against Algeria.

Austria, who beat Jordan in their opening match, were combative if lacking a little quality in the final third, and will still fancy their chances of progressing. But it is the holders who top Group J and look set to top the table in defence of the trophy.

Image: Argentina's Lionel Messi runs away celebrating after scoring the opening goal

The key moments from Dallas...

9 - PENALTY MISS! Messi puts his penalty wide of the post

20 - Messi is through but delays the shot and the chance is gone

23 - Sabitzer's effort is blocked by Romero as Austria threaten

31 - Messi's shot is blocked by Danso after a flick to Martinez

38 - GOAL! Medina's cross finds Messi to dispatch low into the net

57 - Romero suffers a knee injury and is replaced by Otamendi

90+6: GOAL! Messi forces the ball in at the second attempt

Messi reveals anger at penalty

Lionel Messi speaking after Argentina's 2-0 win:

"Beyond anything, I'm so happy for the win. It was huge, tough and difficult. It allows us to be relaxed for what's ahead. All matches in this World Cup are very even, very intense.

"I'm enjoying this moment and craving to enjoy it with my team-mates. There were moments when I was really angry about missing the penalty, but I was able to make up for it."

Analysis: Messi show goes on

Four of Messi's 18 World Cup goals have been penalties but maybe it was more appropriate that the record-breaking effort came as it did. A late run into the box picked out by a smart pull-back and dispatching low into the near corner. Vintage Messi.

He is a different player now. But no less remarkable. In fact, shorn of pace and about to turn 39, it is even more improbable that he is able to do what he does. He has become the first man in over half a century to score in six consecutive World Cup matches.

Much is made of how this team is built to serve him. But the tactic is working. The policy is proving less successful for Portugal, while perhaps Spain could look to Lamine Yamal more than they are doing. Argentina have found the sweet spot.

Image: Lionel Messi scored twice as Argentina progressed with a game to spare in Group J

Image: Lionel Messi's shot map in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria

This was not even Messi's best performance of this World Cup but he could still have scored five. And this was a test. A rare appearance for him of late against European opposition - with Ralf Rangnick's Austria playing a physical, pressing game as well.

It was awkward for Messi and Argentina at times. The space that he had been afforded against Algeria was absent. Sometimes there were five Austria players around him as soon as he received the ball. But that meant there was space elsewhere. He found it.

Image: Lionel Messi's touch map in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria

A first-time pass here, a wriggle free there. It opened the pitch for the penalty won and missed, and the first goal that he scored. Test passed by Argentina. History made by Messi. Eighteen goals now but how many more still to come before the curtain comes down?

A place in the knockout stage has already been booked, although it would be a shock if Messi is not given the chance to add to his total against Jordan. What do you get the man who has everything? Maybe the Golden Boot? The Messi show just goes on and on.

What the result means...

If Argentina finish top of Group J, they will face the runners-up of Group H - currently Uruguay - in the last-32.

Sports.title: Dubois: 'Baumgardner fight will be unavoidable, unmissable and undeniable'
Sports.content:
Caroline Dubois says a fight against Alycia Baumgardner will be "unavoidable, unmissable, and undeniable".

Dubois, who dropped Terri Harper en route to beating her rival world champion by unanimous decision in April returns as the UK's unified WBC and WBO lightweight world champion in a 10-round unified championship defence against American Amelia Moore.

The bout contested at 135lbs with two-minute rounds features on the undercard of MVPW-06 at the bp pulse LIVE arena in Birmingham on August 29, where every fight on the main card will see a UK vs USA contest.

Baumgardner in the pipeline?

Image: Alycia Baumgardner could be in line to fight Dubois

Alycia Baumgardner has previously insisted Dubois still needs to prove herself before the American will agree to fight the unified lightweight world champion.

Dubois has taken aim at Baumgardner and called her out for a high-profile clash, saying the clash "has to happen sooner rather than later".

"She's lost right now," said Dubois. "She's got no opponents. She wanted the Katie Taylor fight but that's not happening, she wanted the Amanda Serrano fight but that's not happening, so who's she going to fight? Absolutely nobody.

"There's no one she can step into the ring with that's on my level. I say that with respect but I know I'm her biggest challenger.

"We're going to build the fight. I want to become undisputed and then she's got no arguments. All we can do is to build and make that fight unavoidable, unmissable, and undeniable. That happens by me becoming undisputed."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Baumgardner believes Dubois is avoiding a fight with her

A 10-round junior middleweight championship unification fight between Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron will headline a main card in Birmingham and Dubois said: "It's a close fight - I'm split. Mikaela Mayer has got a bit more dimensions but then I wake up and think Chantelle Cameron is a beast. She's going to bring the pressure and she has the home advantage.

"It's a 50-50 fight. I know it's going to be a great fight."

'Taylor is the GOAT'

Image: Dubois said she would have loved to have fought Irish icon Katie Taylor

Trainer Shane McGuigan hinted at MVP's interest in a blockbuster showdown with Irish boxing icon Katie Taylor, who is set to end her stellar career with a fight against unbeaten French fighter Flora Pili at Croke Park in Dublin on Saturday September 5.

"Katie Taylor is the GOAT," Dubois said. "She's a champion and she deserves to fight whoever she wants to fight. She sold out 80,000 which is phenomenal. It doesn't matter who is in the corner. This is about Katie Taylor. It's not about the fight!

"She's getting the moment to sail off into the sunset exactly the way she wants to. I'll be supporting her. No one can discredit who she's fought and who she has been in the ring with and her tenacity throughout the years.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Natasha Jonas, who hasn't fought since last March, admits only a 'big occasion' could tempt her back to the boxing ring

"I would 100 per cent be backing myself [if I had the chance to fight her] and it would have been an awesome fight to have. I would have loved to have fought her straight out of the 2012 Olympics.

"It's not going to happen and I'm not focussing on that. If there were no other women to fight then I would be upset, but I've got big names."

Sports.title: Draper 'wins ugly' in Eastbourne opener under new coach Murray
Sports.content:
Jack Draper beat lucky loser Marcos Giron 6-4 7-6 (7-5) in an impressive straight sets first-round victory at the Eastbourne Open in his first game under new coach Andy Murray.

Draper has been hampered by injuries since the US Open last August, with a knee problem causing his latest stint on the sidelines since April.

The former World No 4 returned on the grass of Eastbourne after only playing nine matches throughout 2026 one week before Wimbledon starts with British tennis great Murray as part of his coaching set-up for the first time in competition.

Draper's boost ahead of Wimbledon: 'Murray believes in me and my tennis'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Draper opens up about his recent struggles with injury and hails the impact of new coach Murray

Speaking to Sky Sports on Sunday, Draper revealed that coach Murray had helped him focus on the longer-term picture amid his fight to regain fitness.

"He [Murray] has always supported me," said Draper. "I've always had a great relationship with Andy. We spent some time together towards the back end of his career and he's been a great support to me every since he has stopped as well, but it felt like a really good time to get Andy in my team. I've always wanted that because he's one of my biggest inspirations.

"To have him there in my coaching team, not only as a coach, but a mentor as somebody who has been through it all, which is a special thing. But also the fact that he believes in me, believes in my tennis - especially in this moment now which is to come back and build myself up again. It gives me a big boost!"

'I think I was always pretty good'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tim Henman and Laura Robson discuss Murray joining Draper's coaching team

Murray delivered glowing praise of Draper's ability, hailing his tennis as "b****y good".

"I was thinking to myself, 'I was like No 4 in the world'. I think I was always pretty good," Draper jested. "Hearing that from Andy means on another level, so he's a special, special person, not only as a person, but also his tennis knowledge. If he's saying that about you, then there's no one who you can get more confidence from than him.

"To know someone who has dealt with all the things that you have gone through such as injuries, or pressure moments, or how to deal with certain situations, he really does bring to me so many different things and he delivers it in such a calm way and in a way that is very helpful. He's very honest but also very calm. He has a very good influence on me."

Draper, who has endured an injury-stricken 12 months, said: "I'm so happy to be back at a tournament. It's been way too long. My body is feeling good. It's been a tough time doing rehab and not be able to get on the match court but to come back at a tournament like Eastbourne is great so I'm really happy.

"I always saw injuries as being a one-to-two-week thing, so when you have a big one, you do lose a lot of confidence in your body and doing the thing that you've always been able to do.

"You can go from doing anything to then really struggling just to move without pain or something like that, so you have to work yourself through it. And luckily I've had some really amazing people around to help guide me and tell me, 'Jack, it's going to be alright, you'll get out there' and it's nice to be back."

Venus suffers agonising defeat

Image: Venus Williams is still waiting for her first singles victory of 2026

Venus Williams returned to a grass-court tournament for the first time in three years but the American went down to an agonising 6-2 4-6 7-6 (8-6) to Irina-Camelia Begu in Bad Homburg and is now 0-8 in 2026.

The 46-year old last won a singles match in July 2025 when beating fellow American Peyton Stearns at the Washington Open.

She is the first former No 1 to lose 11 matches in a row since the rankings were first published in 1975.

Meanwhile, Adam Walton defeated Nick Kyrgios 6-3 6-4 to reach the second round in Mallorca.

Kyrgios will play only doubles at Wimbledon with Alexander Bublik.

Osaka breezes through at Bad Homburg Open

Image: Naomi Osaka is through to the Bad Homburg round of 16

Naomi Osaka breezed past Magdalena Frech 6-4 6-1 in an interrupted straight sets win in the first round of the Bad Homburg Open.

The World No 16 leapt out to a 5-0 first set lead, but missed a set point, allowing Frech to make a brief challenge and win four straight games to get herself back in the match before play was interrupted by rain on Sunday night.

Osaka needed just one game after the resumption on Monday to seal the first set, and produced a blistering performance to win six of the next seven games in a 32-minute second set to send the Pole home and book her place in the next round.

"I'm definitely really happy. I haven't played her in an official match before, and this is my first official grass court match of the year," Osaka said.

"I feel like I hit heavy compared to a lot of other girls, so I'm hoping that helps me pull out some victories on this surface."

Sports.title: Can 'familiar face' Maresca carry on Guardiola's work at Man City?
Sports.content:
One of Pep Guardiola's more memorable quotes from his time as Manchester City boss is "we cannot replace him." It was 2021 and a tearful Guardiola was talking about Sergio Aguero - but now it is himself who is being replaced as head coach.

And how do you replace the irreplaceable? Enzo Maresca is set to be the man tasked with taking that specific objective on, with the club closing in on signing the Italian as their new boss.

It's been the worst-kept secret in football, with rumours linking Maresca to the Etihad Stadium dating back to Christmas time, when he was still in charge at Chelsea. But the fallout from his time at Stamford Bridge - which saw him step down after one win in seven games amid boardroom issues - still makes it a little peculiar.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie O'Hara reflected on Man City's pursuit of Enzo Maresca, tipping Luis Enrique as a better successor

But cue another Guardiola quote from 2025. "One of the best managers in the world," he said. That time, he was describing Maresca.

The former Chelsea boss has been picked by City because of his history with the club. Many at the club were impressed with how he handled the role of Elite Development Squad (EDS) head coach - effectively the club's U21s squad - in the 2020/21 season.

Maresca gained plaudits for taking a youth team and bringing the standards and the technical level much closer to the first team. The players he developed include Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer - who have since thrived on a global level.

But the Italian also had an impact with the first team. After a 2021 spell as Parma head coach, which did not go well, Maresca returned to City as one of Guardiola's assistants for just one season. But it was an emphatic one - as City picked up the treble that term.

Image: Maresca (left) spent a season working under Guardiola (right) in the first-team

That season helped create a narrative that Maresca was another Guardiola in the making. Leicester saw it during that treble-winning season, so immediately hired him to win the Championship. Then Chelsea came calling - as his stock rose massively within two years.

The reason why? "Enzo is very similar to Pep," Brian Barry-Murphy told Sky Sports in 2024. Barry-Murphy replaced Maresca as City's EDS head coach and is now in charge of Cardiff City in the Championship.

Because he succeeded Maresca in City's academy structure, the pair worked closely together. He also had the opportunity to observe the Italian's methods first-hand during his time with the City first team.

"When he came back to work as Pep's joint-assistant, he was so active and so involved in the coaching," Barry-Murphy added about Maresca.

Image: Maresca (right) was in Man City's backroom team when Erling Haaland joined the club

"When you work with someone like Pep, he's such a dominant figure. He's so good and commands the respect of everybody, it can be easy to stay in the background and not be super-active.

"But Enzo was coaching from day one and you could see the respect players had for him was instant. That's why he was so important."

Like Mikel Arteta before him, Maresca was right by Guardiola's side, another tactical voice within his inner circle. During the Champions League final, club footage showed Guardiola and Maresca plotting together at half-time on the tactics board, discussing how to break down Inter Milan.

It requires a precise and intense tactical mind to work alongside such a legendary figure - and Maresca was involved in the minute details of City's structure that season.

"They see the game in similar ways," added Barry-Murphy about Maresca's comparisons with Guardiola. "The way they coach is a total dedication to improving the players, so they feel comfortable at what they're asking them to do. That core way of playing and coaching is similar.

"Enzo would be involved in everything. He would be coaching all the players at different times.

Image: Maresca was said to be very involved in Man City training when working under Pep Guardiola

"When you see Pep work so closely like I have, the amount of technical work that goes on daily is the most important thing.

"We all see the tactical outcomes on a Saturday - the innovation that is so acclaimed for Pep. But what we don't see is the amount of work that goes into the technical actions to give the team the confidence to know that no matter what happens on a Saturday, they've worked on those technical concepts every single day of every single week while the season is taking place.

"That's why the level is so high. Enzo was in line with that and was very helpful to the players to improve those technical actions and concepts."

However, while Maresca managed to earn the respect of Man City's playing squad four years ago, there has been a huge overhaul of the City squad since then.

Only Ruben Dias, Nathan Ake, Rico Lewis, Rodri, Phil Foden and Erling Haaland remain from City's treble-winning squad that Maresca worked with. And even then, the futures of Rodri and Ake remain uncertain at the club.

Maresca is taking on a huge City rebuild that not only includes Guardiola's exits - but that of Bernardo Silva and John Stones too. To do that, he will have to channel his inner Guardiola, who has reinvented this City first-team squad a number of times.

But Maresca was not only well-regarded at City, but outside the Premier League too during his time at Chelsea. And not just from his former mentor Guardiola.

Arsenal manager Arteta surprised many in the press room in March of last year, when he made a stunning remark about Maresca's Chelsea after beating them 1-0 at the Emirates.

"In my opinion, they are the best attacking team in the league," Arteta said. "In open play? By a mile."

Image: Arteta and Maresca could be title rivals next season

And Arteta's explanation for it? "Because of the manager they have."

"The stats say it and everything that I've seen say it," the Arsenal manager continued.

"They can open you up, they can run in transition, they have individual quality, any player in the defensive line can throw you in behind, they can combine on both sides, on weak sides."

The numbers provided some more clarity on what Arteta was getting at. While Chelsea were struggling to see out qualification for the Champions League at the time, they ended that campaign as one of the most exciting teams in the league.

Image: Chelsea's stats in their only full season under Enzo Maresca

In the 2024/25 season, Maresca's Chelsea finished top for direct attacks and second for shots from counterattacks - highlighting Arteta's comments about their dangerous moments in transition. Even though that Chelsea team ranked fourth in possession, they had a real energy about them on the ball.

They were also second in the league for big chances created, expected goals and shots on target. It may not quite be the elite standards set by Guardiola in the past - but it's still a solid basis to work with.

And at Chelsea, Maresca was working with a young squad - and still qualified for the Champions League and won a European trophy, plus the Club World Cup.

The way Chelsea's season unravelled under Liam Rosenior showed just how easily the project could have gone - under Maresca, he guided them into the Christmas-time title conversation in each of the past two seasons.

"The job he has done at Chelsea does not get enough credit," said Guardiola about Maresca's achievements during the season just gone.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pep Guardiola reflected on Enzo Maresca's exit from Chelsea, saying it confirmed how lucky the Man City manager is with his role within the team

At City, Maresca will have more than enough experience around him to target the highest honours. Whether he has enough experience himself to guide a seamless transition from Guardiola into a new era remains to be seen.

13m ago 19.49 EDT Back on the pitch, the Iraqis are going into a huddle. They look pumped, which is an achievement in itself after a half-time that has lasted longer than the whole match was meant to. It’s been two hours now. Share

22m ago 19.40 EDT Readers with long memories may dimly recall an email from a dad whose daughters were at the game. That was John Peeler ((23:09). Now here’s a follow-up… “With no football happening on the pitch, fans have resorted to playing in the stadium concourse. Fantastic bout of juggling by the Iraqi fans in here!! “But of course now that i’m writing in, the game’s back on!!!! — Ruby Peeler (yes, daughter of John).“ Share

One compilation of writing I bought there contained a very moving account of a fatality during a storm in a match at (I think) Maidstone. There are cones on the pitch.” A minute later, he emails again. “‘Weather threat has cleared! Football action will soon return!’ says announcer. Players out. Admittedly it is as dark and as wet as at any point this evening, but still!” View image in fullscreen William Saliba decides it’s jumper on weather. Photograph: Hannah Peters/FIFA/Getty Images Share Updated at 19.43 EDT

Thank you on behalf of our readers, who have been doing most of the writing. “An update from the US: the FOX broadcast is now indicating a 7:50PM ET restart.” Great tip-off, Joe, but this is The Guardian: we’re inclined to take Fox with a pinch of salt. If they’re right about this, the whistle will go for the second half in 20 minutes. Share Updated at 19.31 EDT

39m ago 19.23 EDT A few more emails. “Looks like the weather is trying to ensure Messi owns the record outright,” says Pam. “At least for a few days.” “As someone who played a lot of club cricket in the northern leagues,” says Charles Winterton, “I simply don’t understand what all the fuss is about, Just bloody well get on with it.” “Clearing up Philly Stadium?” says Sandgk. “Send in a Kentish man with a dowsing rod to find the true source of the leak.” Share

49m ago 19.13 EDT A thought from Aditya Anchuri. “Time for Duckworth-Lewis?” Share

We thank all fans for their understanding and co-operation.” To paraphrase Harrison Ford … You can type this shit, Gianni, but you sure can’t say it. View image in fullscreen Come on, deem it safe! Photograph: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images Share Updated at 19.13 EDT

1h ago 19.06 EDT The latest quip comes from Johnathan Kaszynski. “These hydration breaks,” he says, “are really getting out of hand.” Share

But she also mentions the possibility of the match being abandoned. And the BBC is abandoning it for now, as it switches from the football to the news. Nothing much has happened in British politics today, has it? Share Updated at 18.59 EDT

1h ago 18.50 EDT “Is there a non-plussed looking groundsman on his way round the pitch,| asks Andy Flintoff, “with a fork to try to assist with drainage? Or a man on a tractor with a supersopper?” Good questions. If there is a man on a tractor, it had better be Ali al-Hamadi. Share

1h ago 18.48 EDT “Given FIFA’s dynamic pricing approach,” says Peter Oh, “shouldn’t the ticket holders at Lincoln Financial Field be charged extra for staying this long?” Share

1h ago 18.42 EDT The match suspension continues for now This half-time has now lasted longer than the first half. It’s been more than 50 minutes. “Anyone from the Midwest or the East Coast could have told Fifa it was a bad idea to have outdoor games during the summer.” says Russell Eberts. “There are basically two weather conditions between late May and mid-August: really hot and humid or thunderstorms. That’s it. Nice days with temperatures below 80 degrees (27C) are anomalies. You might get one once every four or five years.” View image in fullscreen It’s nice and sunny in Miami! Photograph: Patrícia de Melo Moreira/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at 18.46 EDT

1h ago 18.35 EDT “Maybe at some point,” says Bartel Van Kerckhove, “Fifa should decide to host their celebration of capitalism in a country that actually cares about human rights. It might help with the wrath of the weather gods.” Share

2h ago 18.32 EDT “My family and I are wondering,” says Emmling, “what happens in the last round of group matches if there’s a weather delay at one stadium. Does the other game have to pause at the same time, in order to keep it fair?” Good question! Share

2h ago 18.31 EDT “According to Infantino,” says David Wall, “football, and FIFA in particular, can unite the world, bring world peace, find my car keys, turn Coke to Pepsi, and so on. 2h ago 18.29 EDT “Worth noting,” says Bob Kurac, “that Bosnia’s (and indeed Herzegovina’s) goalie’s name is also, in translation, Basil.” Nikola Vasilj, I presume. Share

2h ago 18.22 EDT “It’s amazing,” says Justin Kavanagh, “that FIFA can organize huge, over-the-top pre-game shows, dynamic pricing, and World Cups with a cast of thousands (and that’s just the players), and yet… nobody in the stadium would think of putting a couple of umbrellas in the dugouts for the poor coaches in their Sunday-best suits. 2h ago 18.10 EDT “Tim dearest,” says Mac Millings. “Is Joe Hart suggesting that Basil was at Fawlty for the goal?” Share

Share

It’s not normal.” Share
